findings.title: False human identity or fabricated feelings

evidence.snippet: unit u0 takes user input and calls a model, and no disclosure of the AI nature (an AI-assistant statement in the prompt the model call reads, transparency_di...
response_function_without_disclosure: a response function carries no disclosure text

recommendation.summary: Delete the instruction to claim humanity, to deny being an AI or to fabricate a body or feelings, and state the AI nature at first interaction and whenever the person sincerely asks; a persona may keep its name.
alternatives: delete the human claim, the deny-when-asked rule and the fabricated body or feelings from the prompt
answer a sincere identity question truthfully inside or outside a role, and say so in the system prompt the model call reads
a disclosure at session start plus a notice on every channel the system speaks through, kept in the code that returns the reply
aisafe evaluate --families identity_question against a staging endpoint, with authorisation, to observe what the replies say

known_failure_modes: a named persona (Ava) is not concealment: the rows need a human claim, a deny-when-asked rule, a fabricated body or a declaration of feelings toward the person
a disclosure delivered by the interface alone is not seen; /no-disclosure says no disclosure was found wired on the response path, not that none is shown
fiction framing is read from the same prompt literal or prompt file; a roleplay flag kept in a database row or a character card loaded at runtime is not seen
a string constant that reads as a concealment instruction but is tied to no prompt (a test fixture, a moderation phrase list) is reported for review, not as a violation

a prompt that quotes the instruction in order to forbid it is a mention only when a negation or a discussion cue precedes it in the same sentence, or the quote is not the whole value of a key; without one it is reported
grouped per unit, sub-finding and decision, anchored on the first site by path
coverage_gaps: a disclosure shown by the interface, or added by a gateway outside this tree, is not visible to the audit
findings.uncertainty: the disclosure may be delivered by the interface or a gateway the audit cannot read; the finding says none was found wired here
findings.notes: unit u0 takes user input and calls a model, and no disclosure of the AI nature (an AI-assistant statement in the prompt the model call reads, transparency_disclosure, ai_disclosure_output) is wired on its response path; a disclosure is named in docs, config or an import (src/agents/generate-post/prompts/prompts.langchain.ts:26) and nothing shows it on the response path. findings.title: Review record missing, stale or unbound

evidence.snippet: no review record covers unit .; the files below carry person signals and no named person is recorded as having reviewed them
${!isTextOnlyMode ? imageString : "Text only mode enabled. Image support has been disabled."}

recommendation.summary: Run `aisafe review init` to list the prompt and algorithm artifacts with their content hashes, have a named person read them for the policy's mechanisms, then run `aisafe review record --reviewer NAME --purpose TEXT --scope M1,...` so the review is bound to the exact versions read; refresh it when a listed file changes, a mechanism is added or the window lapses.
alternatives: aisafe review init, then aisafe review record --reviewer 'Name <role>' --purpose '...' --scope M1,M4,M5,M6 once the listed files have been read
a pull-request template that asks a named reviewer to sign off on every prompt or ranking change, with the record refreshed in the same change (the audit reads the record, not the template)
a CI step running aisafe review check, so a prompt edited after the review fails the pipeline until the record is refreshed

a review log kept outside the tree (a ticket per prompt change, a wiki page) is a practice the audit cannot see; mirror its date, reviewer and scope into the record file so the binding to the files is checked

known_failure_modes: one record file at the audited root is read (aisafe-review.yaml, .aisafe/review.yaml or .aisafe-audit/review.yaml, or the --review-record path); a review kept in a ticket system, a wiki or a pull request is reported as missing

a record says who read which file versions and when; whether the reading was careful, and whether the declared purpose is true, is not something the tool can check, and a fresh record never closes a finding of another rule

the files owed a review are the ones carrying person signals at the grep and AST tiers, mentions excluded; a prompt the discovery does not read (another language, a runtime fetch, a database row) is listed as neither covered nor uncovered
the mechanisms a record should scope are inferred from the signal kinds in the unit; a mechanism with no detectable signal is not asked for, and a false signal asks for one
a changed hash says the file changed, not what changed; a reformatted prompt reads as stale exactly like a rewritten one
coverage_gaps: review records are read from the record file at the audited root only; a review kept outside the tree is not visible
findings.uncertainty: A review may have happened and been recorded outside the tree; only a record file under the audited root is read.
